question.text:
Statement 1 — Mother to son: "If you don't do your homework, then you can't watch TV."

  • H = "Do your homework"
  • T = "Can watch TV"

The mother's statement "If you don't do your homework, you can't watch TV" is translated as H IFF T, not merely ¬H → ¬T. Which of the following best explains why?

  1. ¬H → ¬T and H ↔ T are always logically equivalent
  2. The mother implicitly also means "if you DO your homework, you CAN watch TV", making it a biconditional in context
  3. Natural language IF-THEN always means biconditional
  4. ¬H → ¬T is the contrapositive of H → T, which equals H ↔ T
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Statement 1 — Mathematician to student: "If a function is not continuous, then it is not differentiable."

  • C = "The function is continuous"
  • D = "The function is differentiable"

The mathematician's statement "If a function is not continuous, then it is not differentiable" is best symbolized as:

  1. C → D
  2. ¬C → ¬D
  3. D → C 
  4. Both B and C

question.text:
• P = "You get an A on the final exam"
  • Q = "You do every exercise in the book"
  • R = "You get an A in the class"

Which of the following correctly translates: "To get an A in the class, it is necessary for you to get an A on the final."

  1. A. P → R
  2. B. R → P
  3. C. ¬P → ¬R
  4. D. Both B and C

question.text:
• P = "You get an A on the final exam"
  • Q = "You do every exercise in the book"
  • R = "You get an A in the class"

Which of the following symbolic forms correctly translate the statement: "You get an A in the class, but you do not do every exercise in the book." (Select all that apply)

  1. R ∧ ¬Q
  2. ¬Q ∧ R
  3. ¬(Q ∨ ¬R)
  4. R ∧ ¬Q ∧ (P ∨ ¬P)

question.text:
• P = "You get an A on the final exam"
  • Q = "You do every exercise in the book"
  • R = "You get an A in the class"
Which of the following correctly translates: "You get an A on the final, but you don't do every exercise in the book; nevertheless, you get an A in the class."
  1. P ∧ ¬Q ∧ R
  2. P → (¬Q → R)
  3. (P ∧ ¬Q) → R
  4. P ∧ ¬Q ∧ ¬R
